subject: Information Theory
title: Signals Carry Information
description: A quick, practical guide to Signals Carry Information.

hook.text: A lighthouse blinks in the dark. Each pattern of flashes tells ships exactly where the rocks are.

buildup.text: A signal is any physical quantity that varies over time or space to convey information.

discovery.text: Sound waves, radio waves, voltage pulses, and light flashes are all signals carrying structured information.

twist.text: The signal itself has no meaning. Meaning comes from the agreed code between sender and receiver.

climax.text: Shannon separated the engineering problem from meaning. His job: move the signal reliably, not interpret it.

punchline.text: A signal is a pattern. The pattern is the message.
